      Which driving behaviors affect your driving score?
      Going over the limit now and then lowers a trip's score, and doing it on drive after drive brings your weekly average down.
      Harsh braking
      Stopping hard once to avoid trouble is fine. Braking hard on most drives usually means following too closely, and it lowers your score over time.
      Harsh acceleration
      Pulling away hard from lights or junctions across several drives adds up and pulls your weekly score lower.
      Fast cornering
      Taking turns and bends too quickly on a regular basis counts against your score, even when nothing goes wrong.
      Picking up your phone while the car is moving lowers a trip's score, and a habit of it shows up clearly in your weekly report.
      Your weekly report shows which factors influenced your driving score the most, so you can see what to change to get a better score. Harsh braking or acceleration is sometimes the safest option, and your report notes these one-off events when they happen. When they show up week after week, they start to pull your score down.
